bullets.title: Risk-on rally: S&P +1.5%, Nasdaq +2.1%; Mag 7 surges 3%+ on AI capex clarity
bullets.body: US equities finished near session highs with S&P 500 +1.48% and Nasdaq +2.13%; five Mag 7 names closed up 3%+ on AI narrative strength. AMZN hit $3T market cap for the first time (+4.6%), MSFT +4.7%, META +6%, GOOGL +4.9%. JPM notes Mag 7 P/E multiples 2+ standard deviations below 2018–2023 mean, implying ~30–56% upside to fair value on improved ROIC narratives.

bullets.title: ISM Manufacturing hits 4-year high of 55.6, broadening cyclical recovery
bullets.body: July ISM Manufacturing printed 55.6 vs. 54.0 consensus and 53.3 prior — the highest reading since May 2022 and seven consecutive months of expansion. Prices Paid 71.1 remained elevated; employment 52.8 beat. PMI respondents in AI supply chain are optimistic; non-AI respondents less so. July PMIs signal broad demand-driven recovery, not just inventory restocking, supporting higher-rate environment.

bullets.title: Fed: Citadel warns Warsh messaging lacks credibility; hawkish dissenters call for rate hikes
bullets.body: Citadel Securities says Fed Chair Warsh's policy framework creates uncertainty by pledging to curb inflation without explaining how, relying on market yields to tighten. Separately, three FOMC dissenters (Logan, Hammack, Kashkari) favor incremental rate hikes citing sticky inflation, loose financial conditions, and demand-side pressure; Williams viewed July as a close call requiring ≤0.2% monthly core PCE to justify inaction.

bullets.title: Treasury financing $127B above estimates; fiscal doom loop risk if 10Y pierces 5%
bullets.body: Treasury announced $739B Q3 net borrowing ($68B above prior estimate) and $628B Q4 ($19B above JPM forecast), leaving financing needs cumulatively $127B higher than expected. JPM flags upside risk to its $1.96T FY27 deficit forecast; 10Y yield testing 4.71–4.81% support. Separately, a fiscal-rate doom loop note warns that even an orderly 10Y breach of 5% would likely pressure risk assets.

bullets.title: Fed SLOOS: Banks loosened lending standards broadly, pointing to loan growth into late-2027
bullets.body: The Fed's SLOOS survey shows banks eased lending standards in Q3 across C&I, consumer, and residential mortgage segments; broad lending standards historically lead bank loan growth by 5 quarters, suggesting acceleration into late-2027. CRE standards eased but loan demand slipped slightly. Signal is consistent with healthy 2H26 consumption.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler CapEx thesis intact: $900B in 2026, $1.5T in 2027; backlogs +150% YoY
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised global cloud capex forecast to $1.2T for 2027 (+30% YoY, +$170B vs. prior consensus); separate analysis projects $900B in 2026 and $1.5T in 2027 across Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Oracle. JPM notes hyperscaler RPO/backlog grew 150% YoY to ~$1.7T vs. 80% capex growth, with Amazon capacity sold into 2028. AWS CEO notes AI focus shifting from training to inference workloads.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Q2 EPS tracking 45–47% YoY growth but quality of earnings matters
bullets.body: S&P 500 Q2 EPS growth tracking 45–47% YoY (DB estimates 33%, consensus was 22%), but 19% of that growth stems from GOOGL/AMZN equity investment 'other income' gains of ~$151B combined. Ex-those gains, underlying growth is materially lower. Profit margins spiked to record 16.7% — the most mean-reverting series in finance. Deutsche Bank raised 2026 EPS forecast to $358 and 2027 to $420 on 87% beat rate.

bullets.title: Hedge fund July: second-worst gross leverage decline on record; Info Tech net bought
bullets.body: Global L/S managers suffered their second-worst monthly drawdown in four years; Asia L/S saw worst drawdown on record. July saw largest de-grossing since January 2021. Despite the carnage, 9 of 11 US sectors were net bought, led by Info Tech, Consumer Discretionary, and Cyclicals — short covers in North America drove de-grossing activity.

bullets.title: SPX positive gamma dynamics: $1B+ call wall moved to 760 strike; market absorbed 80% of weekly implied move in first 90 minutes
bullets.body: SPY's $1B+ call wall shifted up to the 760 strike on relentless positive gamma, creating a mechanical bid under the market. Separately, SPX absorbed 80% of its 105-point weekly implied volatility range in the first 90 minutes of Monday trading — a sign of compressed realized vol relative to implied.

bullets.title: Technician warns: easy SPX bounce is over; semis not leading, downside protection crushed
bullets.body: Market technicians flag SPX approaching resistance after its initial bounce, with semiconductors notably absent from leadership. Downside protection has been largely eliminated. The NDX fell 6.6% in July — its worst month since March 2025 — but has rebounded ~590bps in 3 sessions, now ~2% from its 50-DMA. SOX dropped from 80% above its 200-DMA in June to just 20% above.

bullets.title: Oil down 5%+ on Iran de-escalation rhetoric; Hormuz risk remains as Iran rejects US proposal
bullets.body: WTI crude fell 5.1% to $80.14 on geopolitical de-escalation signals; bond yields declined 2–3bps across the curve. However, Iran rejected the latest US Hormuz proposal, insisting the strait won't reopen until the war ends. US officials told CBS that contrary to Trump's claims, no new Iran negotiations are planned. US forces redirected 44 vessels through Hormuz and SPR inventories hit lowest since 1983 at 304.8M barrels.

bullets.title: Bond market regime: stock-bond 'Fire' correlation driven by structural factors, not Warsh
bullets.body: A key rates note argues the yield curve steepening (2s20s at 100bps) and term premium rise reflect heavy duration supply in a 'Fire' regime — not new skepticism of Warsh's inflation-fighting credibility. CPI breakeven at 2.25% signals market confidence in 2% PCE target achievement; the regime shift predates Warsh and originated with the escape from the zero bound/inflation burst.

bullets.title: White House invites META, GOOGL, OpenAI, Anthropic to Tuesday AI framework review
bullets.body: META and GOOGL were invited to the White House Tuesday to examine the new AI safety testing framework; the Trump administration also invited staffers from OpenAI, Anthropic, and other major AI companies for the same session. Separately, the White House finalized details of advanced AI model tests and ended the prior voluntary frontier AI model review process.

bullets.title: Chinese AI models advancing rapidly at 100x lower cost; open-source vs. frontier debate intensifies
bullets.body: DeepSeek's new model costs 100x less than Anthropic's flagship; Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max achieved claimed performance parity with Anthropic. BABA shares surged +7.3% on the news. Observers debate whether open-source commoditizes frontier model economics or whether both ecosystems are needed to fund the $1–2T US AI capex buildout. Enterprise adoption still favors Anthropic/OpenAI for governance and compliance reasons.

bullets.title: AI labor disruption modest but increasingly visible; July hiring expected to stay soft
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's AI disruption tracker estimates AI displacement added ~15bp to the unemployment rate as of Jun-26, up from 10bp in Dec-25, with sharper effects on younger workers and AI-exposed occupations. UBS notes companies continue to delay headcount additions in favor of AI efficiency gains, pointing to a continued low-hire/fire labor environment.

bullets.title: Tech IG bonds lost 2.2% in July as yields hit late-2023 highs; BofA issued biggest-ever sell signal
bullets.body: Investment-grade bonds of tech companies lost 2.2% last month with yields rising to highest since late 2023, caught between rate risk and AI capex cost anxiety. Separately, BofA issued what observers characterized as its biggest-ever sell signal even as tech saw the largest weekly inflows in history — the sharpest momentum drawdown since 2008.

bullets.title: Analog/power semis lagging despite strong ISM; MPWR -5%, TXN -3% as AI shifts to data center value
bullets.body: GS TMT desk notes analog and power semis are underperforming despite ISM Manufacturing hitting a 4-year high at 55.6, with MPWR -5% and TXN -3% on the day. The AI trade is rotating from semis to hyperscaler data-center value dynamics, with analysts calling for 'violent upside repricing' in AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL relative to semiconductor names.

bullets.title: Global portfolio allocations shifting toward equities; Goldman notes record equity weighting
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs reports global portfolio allocations are shifting further toward equities, including private markets, with the trend accelerating. Tom Lee (Fundstrat) separately calls for S&P 500 to reach 7,800 in August and sees 2027 as potentially one of the best years for stocks; Deutsche Bank's revised S&P 500 EPS forecasts ($358/2026, $420/2027) support the bullish case.

bullets.title: NVIDIA: Safe Superintelligence $5B raise; HBM4 cost rising to $31-32/GB; Rubin GPU shipments cut to 1M
bullets.body: NVIDIA led a $5B investment in Safe Superintelligence and announced a long-term strategic partnership. Separately, Jefferies cut Rubin GPU shipments to 1M units (from 1.5M) for FY26 but kept total chip shipments roughly flat via higher Blackwell orders; HBM4 cost estimates rose to $31–32/GB from $20/GB, implying significant margin pressure as GPU prices jump to $78–80K.

bullets.title: July FOMC dissent points to higher-for-longer; bond-equity correlation regime key risk to watch
bullets.body: The stock-bond correlation shift to a 'Fire' regime means heavy duration supply is no longer diversifying for equity portfolios. With three hawkish dissenters, the Fed policy toggle remains data-dependent; markets are functioning as FOMC prediction mechanisms. Persistent 10Y above 5% or a Treasury QRA signaling coupon size increases are the key catalysts that could pressure risk assets broadly.
